items.jobTitle: Software Designer – High -Tech Semiconductor Equipment (PLC / C++ / C#)
items.jobDescription:
As a Software Designer – High-Tech Semiconductor Equipment (PLC / C++ / C#), you have experience to design and define PLC, machine control software and higher-level system software for next-generation semiconductor equipment
In this role, you contribute to the development of advanced high-tech semiconductor machines, such as next-generation sintering equipment. You operate across the full stack of machine and system control: from PLC-based machine control (TwinCAT / Siemens) to higher-level software components in C++ or C#.
You work in either an environment where software is developed from scratch or with large legacy source code, which is tightly integrated with hardware and electronics, requiring a balanced skillset across machine control and modern software engineering.
What excites you as a Software Designer – High -Tech Semiconductor Equipment (PLC / C++ / C#)?
As a Software Designer, you work on technically challenging semiconductor equipment where machine control and higher-level software come together. You translate requirements into robust designs, take ownership of modules or subsystems, and ensure a consistent design from the PLC layer up to system software.
From our office in Erlangen, at customer locations, and remotely when appropriate, you enjoy working on:
 Designing and implementing machine control software using PLC technologies (TwinCAT 3 / Siemens) and or SECS/GEM.
 Developing higher-level equipment control software components in C++ and C#.
 Translating system requirements into integrated hardware–software solutions and challenging requirements to drive optimal designs.
 Bridging the gap between control engineering and software engineering disciplines.
 Contributing to the development and evolution of both greenfield and legacy architectures for high-tech machines.
 Integrating, testing, and commissioning complex semiconductor equipment.
 Collaborating within Scrum teams and multidisciplinary engineering groups across software, electronics, and mechanics to deliver high-quality solutions.
 Sounds good so far? We'd love to tell you more…
Your future workplace
This is what you bring to the table
 Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, or a related field, combined with 5–10+ years of experience in high-tech machine building and software development.
 Strong expertise in PLC-based machine control (Beckhoff TwinCAT 3 and/or Siemens) and experience with SECS/GEM combined with solid software development experience in C++ or C#.
 Proven experience designing and implementing control software for complex machines and industrial automation systems.
 Good understanding of Object-Oriented Design, software architecture principles, and requirements engineering, with the ability to translate requirements into effective technical designs.
 Experience working in Agile/Scrum environments and with modern development tools such as Git and Azure DevOps.
 Strong analytical, communication, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to bridge machine control and software domains, challenge unclear requirements, and take ownership of solutions.
 Collaborative and flexible mindset, with willingness to travel within the Netherlands and occasionally across Europe, and to work in a hybrid on-site/remote environment.
 Nice to have: Python, Java, TwinCAT Safety, or industrial robotics experience (e.g., KUKA).
 This is what you can expect in return from Sioux
 Flexible 40 hour working week, with room to work from home
 A healthy work-life balance is very important for us. We have 30 vacation days per calendar year.
 You will work with passionate colleagues who share your drive for technology and business success.
 By combining our expertise in software, electronics, mechanics, mechatronics, mathematics and assembly, we make the impossible possible for our customers and get to work on challenging high-tech projects.
 You get a lot of freedom and responsibility; after all, you know exactly what you are doing.
 Personal coaching and training, so that you can continue to develop yourself.
 We also believe it is important to have fun together. We organize events for our employees, from summer parties for the whole family and lively Christmas celebrations to inspiring knowledge events for the high-tech community.
 Our office in Sioux is ideally located in the heart of the “Medical Valley” in the university town of Erlangen.
 You can share your knowledge with colleagues over lunch, and there are always like-minded people around for a round of darts or table soccer to lighten the mood. Sports are also a big deal at Sioux Technologies Gemany - join our running group or our beach volleyball team.
 High Tech & High Fun
We can tell you all about the typical Sioux culture and the high-tech challenging projects. About how you can develop yourself, like nowhere else. But we’d rather have you hear it from our own employees.
Go to testimonials >
If you want to know more about our challenging projects, please click here.

This position requires access to controlled technology, as defined in the US Export Administration Regulations (15 C.F.R.
 730, et seq.). Qualified candidates must be legally authorized to access such controlled technology prior to beginning work. Business demands may require Sioux to proceed with candidates who are immediately eligible to access controlled technology.

Deine Mission & Herausforderungen
 Wir bauen unsere Legged‑Robotics‑Kompetenz auf NEURAs Quadrupeden weiter aus. Diese Rolle deckt beide Kernschichten des Legged‑Control‑Stacks ab: Trajektorienoptimierung und MPC für kino‑dynamische Bewegungsgenerierung sowie QP‑basierte Instantaneous Whole‑Body Control, um diese Bewegungen mit 1 kHz auf echter Hardware auszuführen.
Der Fokus liegt auf kontaktreicher Dynamik, Echtzeit‑Optimierung und zuverlässiger Ausführung auf physischen Robotern. Du arbeitest eng mit State Estimation, Simulation, Low‑Level‑Control und Hardware‑Teams zusammen – ebenso mit den Applikationsteams, deren Aufgaben am Ende von robuster, vorhersagbarer Lokomotion und stabilem Whole‑Body‑Verhalten abhängen.
 Whole‑Body‑Bewegungsgenerierung und ‑Regelung für Floating‑Base‑Legged‑Plattformen – Lokomotion, Balance, Kontaktübergänge und Loco‑Manipulation (gehen und gleichzeitig manipulieren).
 Trajektorienoptimierung und Model‑Predictive‑Control‑Pipelines über Roboterzustand, Kontaktpläne, Bodenreaktionskräfte, zentroidalen Impuls und Gelenktrajectorien – mit reduzierten Lokomotionsmodellen wie LIPM, SRBD und zentroidaler Dynamik.
 QP‑basierte Task‑Space‑Inverse‑Dynamik, um instantane Whole‑Body‑Control aus MPC‑ und Trajektorien‑Referenzen mit 1 kHz auf dem realen Roboter auszuführen.
 Whole‑Body‑Modellierung der Plattform: Floating‑Base‑Rigid‑Body‑Dynamik aus URDF/MJCF, Gelenkkonfiguration, FK/IK, Jacobianen sowie Massen‑, Coriolis‑ und Gravitations­terme.
 Constraint‑Formulierung über MPC‑ und QP‑Ebene hinweg – Kontakt‑, Reibungs‑, Drehmoment‑, Gelenk‑, kinematische und Stabilitäts‑Constraints – inklusive Task‑Hierarchie‑Design, passend zur Plattform.
 Solver‑Performance‑Arbeit in beiden Ebenen: Warm‑Starting, numerische Konditionierung, Constraint‑Handling und Echtzeit‑Zuverlässigkeit bei 500 Hz bis 1 kHz.
 Deployment, Tuning und Debugging von MPC‑, Trajektorienoptimierungs‑, IK‑ und Invers‑Dynamik‑Pipelines auf physischen Robotern – inklusive plattform­spezifischer Kontaktmodell‑Kalibrierung und Validierung mit realen Roboterdaten.
 High‑Performance‑C++ für Echtzeit‑Ausführung sowie Python‑Tooling für Analyse, Prototyping und Debugging.
 Auf was können wir uns freuen
 MSc oder PhD in Robotik, Regelungstechnik, Maschinenbau, Elektrotechnik, Informatik oder einem verwandten Fach.
 4+ Jahre Hands‑on‑Erfahrung in der Entwicklung von Trajektorienoptimierung, MPC für Lokomotion und/oder Whole‑Body‑Control auf physischen Robotern.
 Sehr solide Grundlagen in Floating‑Base‑Rigid‑Body‑Dynamik und Kontaktmodellierung.
 Sehr gute praktische Kenntnisse zu reduzierten Lokomotionsmodellen (LIPM, SRBD, zentroidale Dynamik oder Äquivalente) und deren Einsatz innerhalb von MPC.
 Starker Background in Optimal Control, beschränkter numerischer Optimierung und Model‑Predictive‑Control für Legged Robots.
 Hands‑on‑Erfahrung mit Whole‑Body‑QP‑/TSID‑Frameworks auf echten Roboterdaten – inklusive QP‑/DDP‑Solver‑Interna.
 Erfahrung im Deployment von Echtzeit‑Control‑, MPC‑ und WBC‑Pipelines mit 500 Hz bis 1 kHz auf Hardware.
 Sehr gutes C++ für Echtzeit‑Robotik‑Software; Python für Analyse, Tooling, Prototyping und Debugging.
 Praxisnahes Verständnis, wie sich Kontaktdynamik, Aktuator‑Limits, Latenz, State‑Estimation‑Fehler, Solver‑Failure‑Modes und Modellabweichungen auf realer Hardware verhalten.
 Kollaborativer Arbeitsstil: gemeinsames Design, konstruktive Code‑Reviews, proaktive Kommunikation und zuverlässige Abstimmung über Control‑, Estimation‑, Simulation‑, Low‑Level‑Control‑ und Hardware‑Disziplinen hinweg. Starkes Teamwork ist für diese Rolle essenziell.
 Nice to have
 Hands‑on‑Erfahrung mit Humanoiden, Quadrupeden oder anderen hoch‑DOF‑Legged‑Robotern.
 Vertrautheit mit Pinocchio, MuJoCo, Crocoddyl, IPOPT, TSID, OCS2 oder ähnlichen Open‑Source‑Tools.
 Hierarchische QPs, gewichtete QPs, Task‑Priorisierung, Kontaktkraft‑Optimierung oder Operational‑Space‑Control.
 Kontaktplanung, Gait‑Optimierung, Balance‑Recovery; CPG‑basierte oder hybride CPG/MPC‑Controller.
 Multi‑Contact‑WBC: Fußkontakte, bimanuelles Greifen oder Base‑Arm‑Koordination.
 Kontaktkonsistente Dynamik und Impact‑bewusste Übergänge in der Regelung.
 Erfahrung mit drehmomentgeregelten Robotern und hochbandbreitiger elektrischer Aktuatorik.
 Publikationen auf RSS, ICRA, IROS oder CoRL im Bereich Legged Locomotion oder Whole‑Body‑Control.

We are seeking an experienced Race Engineer to connect our athletes, teams, and engineering organization, ensuring insights from the highest levels of competition directly influence the next generation of Specialized product
Working across Product Management, Engineering, Applied Technologies, and S-Racing, the Race Engineer will translate athlete feedback, race observations, Retül data, aerodynamic measurements, and performance analysis into actionable insights and engineering requirements and solutions that directly shape future Specialized products.
This role sits at the intersection of engineering, performance, and racing. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable working with elite athletes, world-class engineers, product teams, media, and industry partners. About CuspAI
 CuspAI is the frontier AI company on a mission to solve the breakthrough materials needed to power human progress. While nature took billions of years to perfect molecules, we are harnessing AI to unlock trillion-dollar materials breakthroughs in months, not millennia. Our founding team is the most cited in the world, comprised of world-class researchers in AI, chemistry and engineering.
We are working on some of the hardest and most important challenges including energy, clean water, the future of compute, and carbon capture, and this is just the start of what our 'search engine' for next-generation materials will unlock.
We invite you to be part of a diverse, innovative team at the intersection of AI and materials science, working to create impactful partnerships that drive innovation, scalability, and industry collaboration. This work matters. Your work matters.
 We’re on the cusp of the on-demand materials era. Join us.
 The Role
 We are seeking a Scientific Software Engineer to build and run the systems that connect our AI platform to physical laboratories around the world. Together with the team, you will shape the software layer of our closed-loop discovery workflow: our agents propose experiments, partner labs execute them, and the results feed back into our models to guide the next set of experiments.
This role sits between lab automation and production engineering. You will bring hands-on experience with scientific or lab automation, and the engineering discipline to make those integrations secure, reliable and scalable across many partners.
You will be part of a small team of materials scientists, ML engineers and software engineers, working closely with each other and with our partner labs. You will help define how our AI platform connects to the physical world and shape the tools and practices that link external partner labs to our platform. You will thrive here if you enjoy collaborating across disciplines and learning from people whose expertise differs from your own.
 Your Impact
 You will turn experimental labs into first-class, programmable parts of the CuspAI platform. Every partner you onboard, and every integration you harden, shortens the loop between an AI-generated hypothesis and a validated material.
 What You Will Do
 Help shape how we connect to partner labs around the world, accounting for different levels of automation and AI-readiness, then design, build and operate the services that send experiment requests from our AI agents and reliably bring results back. 
 Build APIs and data models (e.g. FastAPI, Pydantic) for bidirectional lab-to-cloud data exchange. 
 Integrate with lab instruments, robotic platforms, LIMS/ELN systems and scheduling software, translating between disparate formats and CuspAI's data platform. 
 Make integrations reliable at scale: idempotency, retries, queueing, monitoring and alerting across many partners and time zones. 
 Assist with the technical onboarding of new lab partners, assessing their systems and setting up integrations quickly and repeatedly. 
 Collaborate day to day with experimental materials scientists, optimisation experts and engineers on the team, co-designing workflows and feeding lab realities back into platform design. 
 Deploy and run containerised services on cloud infrastructure, with testing and CI/CD as standard. 
 Must Have Skills And Qualifications
 Hands-on experience with lab automation, self-driving labs or other scientific discovery workflows, e.g. instrument control, robotic platforms, or high-throughput experimentation data pipelines. 
 Strong software engineering background, with production experience building and operating backend services. 
 Deep fluency in Python, including typed, well-tested code and API design. 
 Experience designing distributed systems that integrate with external parties: APIs, message queues or event-driven architectures, and data contracts. 
 Solid understanding of security practices for externally facing systems. 
 A collaborative mindset: you enjoy working in a small, multidisciplinary team, and can communicate clearly with experimental scientists, optimisation experts and engineers alike. 
 Bonus Points
 Experimental lab experience in materials science, chemistry or chemical engineering. 
 Experience with workflow orchestration (e.g. Dagster, Flyte, Prefect) or active learning loops. 
 Experience with infrastructure as code (e.g. Terraform) and observability tooling. 
 Security or compliance experience or handling partner IP and confidential data. 
 Experience working across distributed teams and multiple time zones. 
 What we offer
 A competitive salary: We value and reward impact and growth
 Equity in CuspAI: You have a stake in the success of the company
 Time off to stay fresh: 28 days holiday (DE, NL, UK) or 21 days holiday (JP, SG, US), in addition to local public holidays
 ‘Gold Standard’ parental leave: 26 weeks (primary caregiver) and 12 weeks (secondary caregiver) at full pay - we look after you and your family while we work on the most important materials discovery problems together
 Professional development budget: We invest in your career development so you can stay up to date with the latest industry knowledge or add to your skills to increase impact and growth
 Solve meaningful problems: See how your work has a direct impact on advancing materials science and solving sustainability and climate-related problems through the creation and application of bleeding-edge SOTA technology and revolutionary techniques
 True interdisciplinary teamwork: Be part of a deeply collaborative environment bridging AI research, computational chemistry, and experimental science - work with world-class researchers and engineers who enjoy sharing knowledge and supporting each other
 Join us in shaping the future of materials with AI. Together, we can create groundbreaking solutions for a more sustainable world.

items.jobTitle: R&D Control and HIL Test Engineer
items.jobDescription:
The opportunity
Join our R&D Product Development team and help validate the next generation of power conversion and control systems. You will work in a cross-functional environment alongside design, control, embedded software, system engineering, and quality teams to ensure our products meet performance, reliability, and certification expectations.
In this role, you will validate hardware and control functions for power converters and energy storage applications. You will study system behavior under transient and fault conditions, support grid code compliance, and drive end-to-end traceability from requirements through to final validation reports. Your work directly shapes the robustness and certification readiness of products deployed in industrial and renewable energy applications.
To excel, you bring strong testing fundamentals, hands-on experience with HIL systems and lab benches, and the analytical mindset needed to debug signals, logs, and waveforms. You are structured in your documentation, curious about new technologies, and motivated to automate what others would repeat manually.
You will grow by working on real prototypes and productized systems, contributing to test automation frameworks, and collaborating with global engineering teams. You will deepen your expertise across power electronics, control algorithms, and grid compliance while building a strong foundation in certification and quality processes.
How you’ll make an impact
 Define, execute, and maintain validation and verification activities for power electronic products, prototypes, and systems under development.
 Analyze specifications and technical requirements and translate them into structured validation plans, test procedures, and acceptance criteria.
 Execute validation tests in both factory and field environments for prototype and productized power conversion systems.
 Study system stability and response to electrical transients including symmetrical and asymmetrical faults, voltage dips, frequency disturbances, and power oscillation damping scenarios.
 Simulate, validate, and debug control algorithms and assess compliance with applicable grid codes.
 Conduct technical analysis of logs, signals, errors, waveforms, and performance metrics, and generate clear, reusable validation reports.
 Develop and implement test automation frameworks and scripts for lab and HIL-based validation activities.
 Support product certification activities, component approval, and quality assurance processes, ensuring traceability from requirements to final reports.
 Responsible for ensuring compliance with applicable external and internal regulations, procedures, and guidelines.
 Living Hitachi Energy’s core values of safety and integrity, which means taking responsibility for your own actions while caring for your colleagues and the business.
 Your background
 Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Electronics, or a related engineering field.
 Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in power electronics, validation, verification, or related engineering activities.
 Experience in the design of electrical systems and power electronics converters, including their control.
 Strong experience in validation of electronic products and/or embedded software, with hands-on use of test benches, validation setups, and HIL systems.
 Strong knowledge of power converters, especially AC/DC and DC/DC converter topologies.
 Experience with simulation and modeling tools such as PSCAD, Simulink, or PLECS.
 Proven ability to perform technical analysis of system behavior, signals, and performance data, and to prepare structured validation documentation, reports, and traceability records.
 Self-driven, curious, and motivated to learn and apply new technologies.

 Was tragen Sie bei?
 Unsere Stellwerkssoftware steuert Weichen und Signale und muss jederzeit zuverlässig und sicher arbeiten. Masterthesis zur Entwicklung eines selbstlernenden Zuverlässigkeitskonzepts für smarte Strukturen
items.jobDescription:
Smarte und adaptive Systeme können ihren eigenen Zustand kontinuierlich überwachen, Fehler prognostizieren und auf Veränderungen reagieren. Ziel der Masterarbeit ist die Entwicklung und experimentelle Untersuchung eines datengetriebenen Zuverlässigkeitskonzepts am Beispiel eines adaptronischen Biegebalkens zur Schwingungsreduktion. Dabei werden Sensordaten genutzt, um den aktuellen Systemzustand zu bewerten und eine mögliche Degradation bzw. Ausfallwahrscheinlichkeit vorherzusagen. Ergänzend wird kausales Wissen aus einer probabilistischen FMEA (probFMEA) genutzt, um mögliche Schadensursachen zu identifizieren und die datengetriebene Vorhersage erklärbar zu machen. Daraus soll ein geschlossener Ansatz nach dem Prinzip „Messen – Vorhersagen – Erklären – Entscheiden – Handeln“ entwickelt und experimentell demonstriert werden.
 Masterthesis zur Entwicklung eines selbstlernenden Zuverlässigkeitskonzepts für smarte Strukturen (all genders)
 Darmstadt
 Hier sorgst Du für Veränderung 
 Aufbau und Charakterisierung eines Versuchsaufbaus mit adaptronischen Systems mit Sensorik und Aktorik zur Untersuchung von Schwingungen und Degradation.

 Entwicklung eines datengetriebenen Modells zur Zustands- und Zuverlässigkeitsbewertung, z.B. mittels neuronaler Netze oder anderer Machine-Learning-Verfahren.
 Entwicklung einer probabilistischen FMEA und eines kausalen Modells zur Identifikation und Bewertung möglicher Degradationsursachen.
 Kopplung der Ansätze zu einem geschlossenen Zuverlässigkeitskonzept und experimentelle Bewertung hinsichtlich Vorhersagequalität, Erklärbarkeit und Potenzial für adaptive Maßnahmen
 Hiermit bringst Du Dich ein 
 Studium im Bereich Maschinenbau, Mechatronik, Elektrotechnik, Computational Engineering, Systems Engineering oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung.

 Gute Kenntnisse in Datenanalyse und Programmierung, vorzugsweise Python oder MATLAB.
 Grundkenntnisse in Machine Learning, Statistik oder probabilistischen Methoden sind von Vorteil.
 Selbstständige, analytische und experimentelle Arbeitsweise sowie Interesse an der Verbindung von Simulation, Experiment und KI

Das Fraunhofer-Institut für Optronik, Systemtechnik und Bildauswertung ist mit rund 800 Mitarbeitenden an sechs Standorten eines der größten Fraunhofer-Institute. Das Fraunhofer IOSB-INA in Lemgo, als Standort für die industrielle Automation des IOSB, bietet ein überaus attraktives Arbeitsumfeld in einer hochinnovativen Schlüsselbranche. Wir sind eine der führenden Forschungseinrichtungen in dem Technologie-Netzwerk „Intelligente technische Systeme Ostwestfalen Lippe it’s OWL“ und ein wichtiger Bestandteil der dynamischen Wissenschafts- und Wirtschaftsregion Ostwestfalen-Lippe. Unsere Mission: "Empowering our Partners for the Digital Age".
Die Arbeitsgruppe Cybersicherheit des Fraunhofer IOSB-INA ist ein interdisziplinäres Team aus Experten in den Bereichen Automatisierungstechnik, industrielle Produktion, Cybersecurity und künstlicher Intelligenz. Im Rahmen des Lernlabors Cybersicherheit – einem Weiterbildungsverbund von Fraunhofer und Fachhochschulen – entwickeln wir praxisnahe IT-Sicherheitstrainings, die neuestes Forschungswissen direkt in die Anwendung bringen.
 Wir suchen Verstärkung im Bereich Weiterbildung und Schulung in der Cybersicherheit mit Large Language Models.
 Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung 
 Die Ausschreibung richtet sich an berufserfahrene Personen mit Interesse am Gebiet der Cybersicherheit und Large Language Models. Zu Ihren Aufgaben gehören unter anderem:

Das Fraunhofer FHR in Wachtberg bei Bonn ist Teil der Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft und eines der führenden und größten europäischen Forschungsinstitute auf dem Gebiet der Hochfrequenzphysik und Radartechnik.
Der Bereich „Radar zu Weltraumlageerfassung“ (RWL) entwickelt vor dem Hintergrund der zunehmenden Bedrohung von Satelliten Radarsysteme und Verfahren Weltraumlageerfassung. In zwei Abteilungen vereinen sich unsere Expertisen in den Teilbereichen Radararchitekturen und Verfahren zur Weltraumbeobachtung, als auch Radarsysteme und operationeller Betrieb. Zur Unterstützung der Arbeiten betreibt der Bereich mit dem TIRA (Tracking and Imaging Radar) eine der weltweit leistungsfähigsten Großradaranlagen.
Die Abteilung „Radararchitekturen & Verfahren zur Weltraumbeobachtung“ (RVW) befasst sich mit Forschungsthemen zur Aufklärung und Überwachung von Objekten im erdnahen Weltraum mit Radar. Dazu entwerfen wir innovative Verfahren zur Detektion, Ortung, Bahngewinnung und Radarabbildung bis hin zu Methoden zur Analyse und Identifizierung von Weltraumobjekten. Zum experimentellen Nachweis und zur Anwendung dieser Verfahren entwickeln wir Instrumente für unsere Großradaranlage TIRA und Systemarchitekturen für zukünftige Radarsysteme.
Die Gruppe „TIRA - Signalverarbeitung & Digitale Systeme“ (TIRA-SVDS) entwickelt mit einem interdisziplinären Team aus Ingenieuren, Informatikern und Wissenschaftlern innovative leistungsfähige Radarinstrumente. Neben dem Gesamtsystementwurf und seiner Modellierung sind die Radarsignalerzeugung und -aufzeichnung sowie die echtzeitliche als auch operationelle Signalverarbeitung Kernkompetenzen der Gruppe. Weiterhin beschäftigt sich TIRA-SVDS mit den zum Einsatz der Radarinstrumente erforderlichen Hardware- und Softwarelösungen. Die Gruppe verifiziert die Arbeiten durch die Konzeption, Durchführung und Analyse von Experimenten mit der Großradaranlage TIRA.
Im Rahmen aktueller Forschungs- und Technologieprojekte wird die Großradaranlage TIRA grundlegend modernisiert und um neue Fähigkeiten sowie Systeme erweitert. Gemeinsam mit Ihren Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus Wissenschaft und Technik arbeiten Sie interdisziplinär an anspruchsvollen Entwicklungsaufgaben. Sie entwickeln, integrieren und optimieren moderne Radarsysteme zur Weltraumbeobachtung und ihrer Unterbaugruppen - von der Architektur und Signalverarbeitung bis zu Software, Tests und Validierung.
 Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung 
 Entwurf und Auslegung von Radarsystemen und deren Untersystemen
 Entwicklung von Systemarchitekturen, Schnittstellen und Signalverarbeitungskonzepten
 Implementierung und Integration von Radarsoftware und Algorithmen
 Durchführung von Simulationen, Tests, Messungen und Validierungen
 Analyse und Optimierung der Systemperformance
 Erstellung technischer Dokumentationen sowie Zusammenarbeit mit angrenzenden Fachbereichen
 Hiermit bringen Sie sich ein 
 Erfolgreich abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium in Elektrotechnik, Nachrichtentechnik oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
 Erfahrung in der Entwicklung und Implementierung technischer Systeme, idealerweise im Radar- oder Hochfrequenzumfeld

items.jobTitle: Wissenschaftl. Mitarbeit (m/w/d) - Bi- und multistatische Radarverfahren in der Weltraumaufklärung
items.jobDescription:
Das Fraunhofer FHR in Wachtberg bei Bonn ist Teil der Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft und eines der führenden und größten europäischen Forschungsinstitute auf dem Gebiet der Hochfrequenzphysik und Radartechnik.
Der Bereich „Radar zu Weltraumlageerfassung“ (RWL) entwickelt vor dem Hintergrund der zunehmenden Bedrohung von Satelliten Radarsysteme und Verfahren Weltraumlageerfassung. In zwei Abteilungen vereinen sich unsere Expertisen in den Teilbereichen Radararchitekturen und Verfahren zur Weltraumbeobachtung, als auch Radarsysteme und operationeller Betrieb. Zur Unterstützung der Arbeiten betreibt der Bereich mit dem TIRA (Tracking and Imaging Radar) eine der weltweit leistungsfähigsten Großradaranlagen.
Die Abteilung „Radararchitekturen & Verfahren zur Weltraumbeobachtung“ (RVW) im Bereich RWL befasst sich mit Forschungsthemen zur Aufklärung und Überwachung von Objekten im erdnahen Weltraum mit Radar. Dazu entwerfen wir innovative Verfahren zur Detektion, Ortung, Bahngewinnung und Radarabbildung bis hin zu Methoden zur Analyse und Identifizierung von Weltraumobjekten. Zum experimentellen Nachweis und zur Anwendung dieser Verfahren entwickeln wir Instrumente für unsere Großradaranlage TIRA und Systemarchitekturen für zukünftige Radarsysteme.
Im Rahmen aktueller Forschungs- und Technologieprojekte wird die Großradaranlage TIRA grundlegend modernisiert und um neue Fähigkeiten sowie Systeme erweitert. Gemeinsam mit Ihren Kolleginnen und Kollegen aus Wissenschaft und Technik arbeiten Sie interdisziplinär an bi- und multistatischen Radarverfahren für die erdgebundene, bildgebende Weltraumaufklärung. Der Schwerpunkt liegt auf der wissenschaftlichen Bewertung und systemnahen Ausgestaltung multistatischer Radarsysteme - von der Konzeption und Erprobung bis zur Auswertung.

 Entwicklung und Bewertung von Verfahren zur zeitlichen, frequenzbezogenen und phasenbezogenen Synchronisierung verteilter Radarsensoren
 Erarbeitung interner und externer Kalibrierkonzepte für Antennen, Sende- und Empfangspfade sowie das Gesamtsystem
 Analyse der Auswirkungen von Bahn-, Lage-, Zeit- und Frequenzfehlern auf Bildqualität und Aufklärungsleistung
 Entwicklung und Bewertung von Verfahren zur bistatischen und multistatischen Bildrekonstruktion
 Untersuchung bistatischer und multistatischer Beobachtungsgeometrien unter Berücksichtigung von Leistungs-, Sensitivitäts- und Fehlerbudgetanalysen
 Konzeption und Begleitung von Labor-, Feld- und Demonstrationsexperimenten

items.jobTitle: Konstruktiver Entwurf einer elektromechanischen Deichsel für den Transport autonomer Feldroboter
items.jobDescription:
Große vollautonome Feldroboter müssen zu ihrem Einsatzort transportiert werden, meist mit Zugfahrzeugen oder Transport-anhängern. Aufgrund des hohen logistischen und personellen Aufwandes entstehen hohe Kosten. Eine elektro-mechanische Deichsel könnte den Transportprozess optimieren, indem sie ein Führungsfahrzeug mit dem Feldroboter (nahezu) kraftfrei koppelt. Ein Messsystem erfasst hierzu die Fahrbewegungen des Führungsfahrzeugs und erzeugt Steuersignale für die Feldroboter. In Kombination mit der Wirkung eines Feder-Dämpfer-Systems in der Deichsel werden über diese kaum Zug- und Druckkräfte übertragen. Das Führungsfahrzeug, z. B. ein Pick-up, bleibt bautechnisch unverändert. 
 Hier sorgst Du für Veränderung 
 Zunächst werden für die elektro-mechanische Deichsel funktionale Anforderungen formuliert und Hauptbaugruppen erarbeitet. Für die Hauptbaugruppen sind Arbeitsprinzipien und Wirkmechanismen zu entwerfen und ihre Eignung gemäß den funktionalen Anforderungen zu prüfen und zu bewerten. Nach der Auswahl einer Vorzugslösung ist ein konstruktiver Entwurf zu erarbeiten. Die zu erarbeitende konstruktive Lösung umfasst die Hauptbaugruppen, die Integration notwendiger Sensoren (z. B. Winkelsensoren an den Koppelpunkten) und der Entwurf mechanischer Koppelelemente am Führungsfahrzeug und am Feldroboter 
Die Aufgabenstellung ist für Masterarbeiten und Diplomarbeiten geeignet und lässt sich inhaltlich gemeinsam mit der betreuenden Hochschule und dem Studenten oder der Studentin anpassen.

items.jobTitle: Engineer (f/m/x) - for AI-based system dynamics and control engineering (Oberpfaffenhofen)
items.jobDescription:
The Institute of Vehicle Concepts (FK) of the German Aerospace Centre (DLR) is internationally recognised for the design of future road and rail vehicles that enable climate and environmentally friendly mobility while being affordable and user-friendly at the same time. We research and demonstrate the required key technologies and maintain close cooperation with other scientific institutions as well as industrial and political bodies.
 What to expect 
 We are looking for you to join our team in developing model- and learning-based simulation and control methods for robotic electric vehicles with X-by-wire architectures, in which the driver has no direct mechanical control over systems such as the steering. The high complexity associated with this technology, as well as the requirements for fault tolerance, are the driving forces behind the development of so-called surrogate models, which are intended for use in virtual training via reinforcement learning, among other applications. In your new role with us, you’ll work together with a dynamic, multidisciplinary team to bring your ideas to life. You’ll have the opportunity to develop and experimentally test the latest methods in system dynamics and control engineering—both virtually and on test beds—thereby making a decisive contribution to our mission
 Your tasks 
 analysis, development, and critical evaluation of scientific methods for nonlinear model-based and AI-based control methods
 development of machine learning algorithms, such as reinforcement learning and physically-based neural networks, for the control and simulation of mechatronic systems
 design of “AI-Aided Control Systems Engineering” toolchains based on technologies such as LLMs, Agentic-RAG, and MCP
 scientific analysis of methods for evaluating the robustness and reliability of model- and learning-based control methods
 experimental testing of the methods on near-production and experimental DLR test vehicles with by-wire control, and scientific evaluation of the tests using objective, numerical criteria, as well as assessment of these methods against the state of the art
 authoring scientific publications for international journals and conferences, as well as on the department blog
 Your profile  
 a completed academic degree (Master’s or university diploma) in engineering in the fields of electrical engineering, computer science, robotics, or mechanical engineering with a focus on control engineering/information/automation technology, or other degree programs relevant to the position
 advanced expertise in control engineering and optimization techniques that goes beyond the content of introductory courses
 knowledge of at least one programming language: Modelica, MATLAB, C, or Python
 knowledge of machine learning methods (supervised and unsupervised learning)
 knowledge in the field of automotive engineering and electric mobility
 We look forward to getting to know you!

items.jobTitle: Promotionsstelle "Improving Motion Simulation Experience using Reinforcement Learning" (Oberpfaffenhofen)
items.jobDescription:
Herzlich willkommen am Institut für Flugsystemtechnik. Im Zentrum unserer Arbeit steht das Zusammenspiel von Flugzeugkonfiguration, Pilotinnen und Piloten und moderner Flugsystem-Technologie. Von der Flugdynamik bis zu unbemannten Luftfahrzeugen, von der Simulation bis zum realen Flugversuch – wir analysieren, testen und entwickeln Innovationen, die das Fliegen der Zukunft prägen. 
 Das erwartet dich 
 Bewegungssimulation wird in vielen Bereichen der Forschung und Entwicklung, aber auch zur Ausbildung (z.B. Pilotentraining) eingesetzt. Um dem Simulatorinsassen ein realistisches Empfinden zu vermitteln, wird ein sogenannter Motion Cueing Algorithm (MCA) genutzt, der die Bewegungen von der simulierten Anwendung in den meist deutlich kleineren Arbeitsraum der Bewegungsplattform transferiert. Dabei werden Eigenheiten der menschlichen Bewegungswahrnehmung ausgenutzt, wie Wahrnehmungsschwellen und die Dominanz des optischen Flusses. Da die Bewegungsplattform physikalische Beschränkungen hat und jeder Mensch unterschiedlich empfindet, ist die Suche nach einem immersiven Motion Cueing Algorithmus und dessen Parametrisierung ein herausforderndes Unterfangen.
 Deine Aufgaben 
 Einarbeitung in den bestehenden RL-MCA
 Durchführung einer Recherche, wie die Simulationsgüte quantifiziert werden kann
 Erstellung einer Metrik zur Quantifizierung der Simulatorgüte
 gegebenenfalls Durchführung von Studien zur Bestätigung der Metrik mit verschiedenen MCA
 Entwicklung von Methoden zur schnellen Parametrisierung des Reinforcement Learning MCA
 Entwicklung eines RL basierten MCA, der den bisherigen erweitert, beispielsweise um die Nutzung eines Modells des Vestibulärsystems, die Betrachtung von mehr als sechs Achsen und die Berechnung im Gelenkwinkelraum anstelle des kartesischen Raums
 Das bringst du mit 
 abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium im Bereich Informatik oder Ingenieurswissenschaften
 fundierte Kenntnisse im Bereich Machine Learning
 Programmierkenntnisse in C++, Python
 Erfahrungen im Bereich Bewegungssimulation

 Gute Deutsch- und Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift

 Erfahrung mit Automatisierung, Datenpipelines, ETL‑Prozessen

StellDirVor is an independent consulting, trade and technology company specializing in immersive technologies for healthcare. We support organizations in implementing digital innovations — Virtual, Augmented and Mixed Reality as well as AI — particularly for learning, training and real-time assistance in clinical and care environments. By combining technology and healthcare, we help optimize processes, improve knowledge transfer and enhance quality of care.
 Supported by a Germany (ZIM) and Taiwanese (GIPIP) partnership grant, we are currently developing ARAIAS — an AR- and AI-based hands-free training and assistance system for chronic wound care. Using AR smart glasses, the system enables 3D capture, AI-supported analysis, and standardized remote expertise and documentation directly at the point of care.
 As our ML Engineer (Computer Vision & ML Ops), you will build the AI capabilities at the core of ARAIAS: evaluating and fine-tuning computer vision models on smart glasses data, running the ML operations behind them, and applying generative AI to create synthetic medical images for education. We're at an early stage — moving from concept to working prototype — so the near-term focus is on validating models and building toward a proof of concept we can test in real education and clinical settings.
 As part of a small team, you will own the full data lifecycle end to end — from sourcing, consent and annotation to preparation — alongside model development and deployment.
 We welcome candidates at different experience levels. What matters most is a solid ML foundation and genuine awareness of the medical imaging domain.
 Notes:
 Due to the nature of the project, we can only consider candidates who are already residing in Germany.
 Tasks
 Select and benchmark pre-trained models and/or validated architectures for medical image analysis and adapt them to domain-specific data, ensuring robust performance under real-world conditions
 Identify and adapt suitable generative AI models to create realistic synthetic medical images for education and training
 Evaluate and fine-tune small language models (SLMs) for voice interaction — speech-to-text, intent understanding and text-to-speech — optimized for low-latency or on-device use with smart glasses
 Research and assess state-of-the-art ML models and emerging trends, including Explainable AI (XAI), cybersecurity for ML, and deployment and distribution modes (edge vs. cloud, federated learning, model compression)
 Plan and execute the ML operations pipeline — data gathering, annotation, preparation, training, testing and deployment
 Propose a data collection strategy — research suitable public and clinical data sources, recommend patient consent and other administrative requirements for ML training (e.g., data protection agreements, ethics approval), and define collection and annotation protocols with clinical experts, including labeling guidelines and quality checks
 Identify and validate factors that affect model performance — image conditions, dataset bias, patient diversity, data privacy and regulatory requirements
 Define test strategies and metrics, and validate model outputs against clinician assessments
 Perform build vs. buy analyses for models, tools and services, including cost comparison
 Estimate compute and training costs and propose budgets for model training and deployment
 Choose and set up training environments flexibly — local hardware or cloud — based on cost, data privacy and performance
 Make pragmatic technical decisions appropriate for the current prototyping stage and document results clearly
 Maintain clear, traceable documentation of data sources, models, experiments and design decisions to support audits and quality reviews
 Evaluate and integrate additional sensors where feasible (e.g., depth, LiDAR, thermal, multispectral) and fuse them with RGB input
 Requirements
 Must-Have
 Degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Biomedical Engineering, Mathematics or a related field — or equivalent practical background
 Strong Python skills and hands-on use of PyTorch, OpenCV or TensorFlow
 Solid understanding of computer vision — classification, object detection and image segmentation, 3D Reconstruction and Multi-View Geometry
 Hands-on knowledge of transfer learning — adapting pre-trained models and fine-tuning them on custom datasets
 Working knowledge of the full ML lifecycle — data preparation, training, evaluation and deployment
 Basic knowledge of generative models (diffusion models or GANs) and common open-source libraries
 Comfortable training models both locally (GPU workstation) and on cloud platforms

 Awareness of medical imaging challenges — limited data, label variability between clinicians and class imbalance
 Awareness of healthcare data privacy and ethics (e.g., GDPR, patient consent, anonymization) and why explainability and bias matter in clinical AI

 Self-directed and pragmatic — able to take initiative and own problems end-to-end in a lean team
 Fluent in English — German is a bonus
 Strong Plus
 Projects or coursework in medical imaging or clinical AI
 Familiarity with semi-supervised learning — leveraging limited or partially labeled data
 Experience with 3D data processing — depth maps, point clouds or mesh reconstruction
 Exposure to multi-modal learning — combining RGB and depth or LiDAR data
 Edge AI or wearable deployment (e.g., TensorFlow Lite, ONNX, model quantization)
 Knowledge of explainability methods (e.g., Grad-CAM, SHAP) or adversarial robustness
 Familiarity with MLOps tools (e.g., MLflow, Weights & Biases, DVC, Docker)
 Awareness of medical device regulation for AI software (e.g., EU MDR, IEC 62304)
 Familiarity with small language models (SLMs) and speech pipelines (e.g., Whisper, on-device speech recognition and text-to-speech)

items.jobTitle: Sr. Forward Deployed AI Engineer (Remote Eligible in the UK)
items.jobDescription:
For over 20 years, Smartsheet has empowered teams to manage work seamlessly and scale solutions smarter. Now, in our most ambitious chapter yet, we are uniting human teams with AI agents. By orchestrating the work agents do best, automating manual tasks and uncovering insights at scale, we create the space for people to focus on what truly matters: judgment, creativity, and big thinking. That is magic at work, and it’s what we show up for every day.
 You independently lead the most complex AI deployments Smartsheet undertakes. You own the full engagement lifecycle from technical discovery through production deployment through solutions org handoff. You architect multi-agent solutions, design client-personalized MCP resource packs, and build the Deployment Kits that transform how 200+ solutions consultants and partners operate. You mentor junior FDEs, drive the intelligence loop, and present field findings at weekly Applied AI strategy sessions. You are building a function, not filling a role.
 What You Will Do 
 Lead complex, multi-system AI deployments end-to-end scope, architect, build, validate, and manage the customer relationship throughout.
 Own the AI workshop program for your pod, customize modules per customer, lead technical sessions, translate outputs into production requirements, evolve content from field learning.
 Architect multi-agent solutions selecting the right coordination pattern for each customer’s workflow characteristics and compliance requirements.
 Design client-specific and industry-specific MCP resource packs that serve personalized intelligence from the server so every connected AI surface gets smarter for that customer automatically.
 Own Deployment Kit quality for your pod. If a kit is not documented well enough for a solutions consultant with no engineering background to follow, it isn’t done.
 Lead Solutions Enablement Sprints: transfer AI deployment patterns to solutions consultants and partners with training materials and certification criteria.
 Drive the intelligence loop: author strategic memos, present field findings weekly, contribute Agent Bricks and Skills, file RFCs for platform improvements.
 Mentor junior FDEs on customer engagements, code reviews, and Deployment Kit quality.
 Required 
 6–10+ years production software engineering, including 3+ years deploying AI/ML to production. Deep Python; strong TypeScript/JavaScript.
 Proven track record leading complex enterprise technical engagements. You’ve managed customer relationships, navigated security reviews, and delivered production systems organisations depend on.
 Deep production LLM experience: multi-agent orchestration, MCP/tool-use, RAG optimisation, evaluation frameworks, agent deployment at scale.
 System architecture expertise spanning enterprise systems, cloud infrastructure, and AI services explainable to a CIO and a junior engineer.
 Demonstrated ability to create reusable technical assets that others use in production. You think in platforms, not projects.
 Strong written and verbal communication. Architecture documents, runbooks, strategic memos, training materials. Your Deployment Kits are your portfolio.
 You leave teams better than you found them. You make sure the people you work with understand what was built, why it works, and how to own it without you.
 Ability to travel.  This role requires domestic and international travel approximately 25–50% of the time.
 Elligible to work in the UK on an ongoing basis
 BS or MS in Computer Science, a related field, or equivalent industry experience
 Nice to Have:  
 Experience founding or scaling an FDE/solutions engineering function. 
 Technical founder background. Databricks, AWS Bedrock, or Temporal experience. 
 Deep domain knowledge in healthcare, financial services, or government. Agent framework contributions (Strands SDK, LangChain, open-source MCP servers).
 Proficiency in German/French language will be an added advantage
 Familiarity of AI governance, ethics, and regulatory requirements (e.g. GDPR, UK/EU AI Act) 
 Get to Know Us: 
 At Smartsheet, your ideas are heard, your potential is supported, and your contributions have real impact. You’ll have the freedom to explore, push boundaries, and grow beyond your role. We welcome diverse perspectives and nontraditional paths—because we know that impact comes from individuals who care deeply and challenge thoughtfully. When you’re doing work that stretches you, excites you, and connects you to something bigger, that’s magic at work. Let’s build what’s next, together.

Normal Computing | Build with Us 
 Normal is an applied AI company solving the hardest problems in AI and silicon. We build foundational hardware and software for the semiconductor industry, critical AI infrastructure, and the broader systems that power our world, in partnership with the world's most advanced institutions. We work as one team across New York City, Silicon Valley (Mountain View), and London.
 The Role 
 Validating conventional silicon is a solved discipline. Validating silicon that computes with noise is not, and you will be the one who figures out how. As our FPGA Design Engineer, you will own the bridge between RTL and physical silicon: bringing our physics-inspired ASIC designs to life on FPGA platforms for pre-silicon validation and early software development, and building the test infrastructure for post-silicon bring-up and characterization. Your scope spans the entire FPGA lifecycle: selecting hardware platforms, implementing complex RTL, debugging in the lab, and writing the software that drives it all, working daily with our silicon, EDA, and research teams.
 What You Will Own 
 FPGA Platform Ownership : Lead the selection, procurement, and bring-up of FPGA prototyping platforms (e.g., HAPS, VCU118/VPK180-class boards, or custom hardware) for pre-silicon RTL validation and software development.
 RTL Implementation : Adapt and implement complex ASIC RTL onto FPGA targets, including multi-clock-domain architectures, CDC bridges, and timing closure on dense designs.
 IP Integration : Integrate in-house designs with third-party and vendor IP; serve as the expert on the AMD/Xilinx ecosystem (Vivado IP Integrator, transceivers, memory controllers).
 High-Speed Interfaces : Design, implement, and validate high-speed I/O with a focus on PCIe: our accelerators ship as PCIe cards in standard servers.
 Post-Silicon Validation : Build FPGA-based "tester" designs for silicon bring-up, device characterization, and automated test environments.
 Hardware-Software Stack : Develop the software layer around the hardware: Python/C++ hardware abstraction, register-map generation, and automated build and regression flows.
 Lab Debug : Root-cause complex timing and functional issues in real time using ILA/Vivado Analyzer, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, and BER/eye-diagram characterization of high-speed links.
 What Makes You a Great Fit 
 Proven industry experience taking FPGA designs from RTL through timing closure to validated hardware, ideally in an ASIC prototyping, emulation, or high-growth hardware environment.
 Expert-level SystemVerilog and/or VHDL for synthesis, with deep proficiency in Xilinx Vivado (synthesis, place & route, timing closure, IP catalog).
 Hands-on experience implementing and debugging PCIe, plus AXI/AHB, SPI, UART, JTAG, and other common interfaces.
 Strong Python for automation, test, and build tooling.
 Strong board-level bring-up and lab debugging skills on real hardware.
 Startup mindset: you work independently, pivot quickly, and run at ambiguous problems that span hardware, software, and physics.
 Bonus Points 
 Verification frameworks like Cocotb or UVM
 Experience deploying ML models to FPGAs (hls4ml, FINN, or custom NN-to-RTL flows), or building real-time, sub-microsecond signal processing pipelines.

 How we work

 We organise around problems, not permanent teams. Small pods , usually of two to four Product Engineers, form around the highest-value problem, own it end-to-end from discovery through to running it in production, and re-form as priorities change. Pods sit inside value streams, each owning a customer outcome and led by a Stream Lead who decides which problems the stream takes on and holds the bar for what ships.  Designing and delivering robust production systems where correctness, performance, and resource efficiency matter, with the tests and observability that make complex behaviour safe to evolve.
 Working across the codebase wherever the problem leads, including areas your pod doesn't steward, with stewards looped in proportionate to the risk rather than handing work off and waiting.

 About the role 
 Every airframe Harmattan AI flies starts with a model. System identification turns flight data into the verified dynamics that guidance and control are designed, tuned and trained on. It is the foundation of an autopilot that adapts across multirotors, fixed wings, VTOLs and missiles.
 As a System Identification Engineer, working out of Paris, you will own the path from flight test to identified model. You will design and run your own experiments, build a repeatable identification pipeline, and deliver models the G&C team can trust.
   Responsibilities 
 Experiment Design & Flight Test: Plan and run your own identification tests, from excitation design to flight tests, including coordinating with the .
 Model Identification: Identify rigid-body, aerodynamic, propulsion and actuator dynamics using frequency and time-domain methods, including closed-loop identification on vehicles flown under a controller.
 Propulsion & Actuators: Characterize motors, ESCs, propellers and control surfaces, including bandwidth, delays, saturation, and thermal and battery effects.
 Identification Pipeline: Build and maintain an automated, reproducible pipeline from flight logs to identified model. This covers ingestion, data-quality checks, estimation, validation and reporting.
 Model Validation: Validate models against held-out flight data, quantify uncertainty, and make sure each model is fit for purpose: controller design, simulation, or training learned G&C.
 New Airframes: Extend the capability from multirotors to control-surface multirotors, fixed wings, tail-sitters and missiles.

 System Identification: Proven experience identifying dynamic models of flying platforms from real data, in both the frequency and time domain, including the pitfalls of closed-loop data.
 Flight Mechanics & Control: Solid grasp of rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamic forces and moments, non-dimensionalization, stability modes and propulsion models. Also enough control background to know what the model will be used for.
 Flight Testing: Hands-on experience planning and running flight tests and working from raw, imperfect logs.
 Software: Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with the discipline to build tools others can rerun.

 Fixed-wing aerodynamic modeling; VTOL or tail-sitter dynamics; remote pilot certification; experience with real flight logs; structural or vibration modes; data-driven or learned dynamics models.

 About the Role 
 As a Drone System Validation Technician and Pilot , you will be at the front line of our quality, safety, and reliability efforts. Your primary mission is to ensure that our defense-grade products meet rigorous operational standards before they are cleared for active duty.
 Working within a dedicated flight testing team, you will manage, prepare, and operate fleets of newly assembled drones or related product during intensive field validation campaigns. By logging massive operating hours, you will actively hunt for rare, hard-to-replicate system bugs and edge-case anomalies. We are looking for operators who combine rigorous testing discipline with the hands-on piloting expertise required to accurately assess and validate nominal drone behavior in flight. Your technical feedback will directly enable our engineering teams to secure and polish our next-generation defense systems.
   Responsibilities 
 Intensive Flight Testing: Conduct high-volume flight testing of newly assembled interceptors to log hours, validate systems, and actively hunt for rare, intermittent flight anomalies.
 Aviation Performance Assessment: Manually operate, stress-test, and critically evaluate the flight dynamics of various platforms (multirotors, fixed-wing, flying wings, and RC planes) to ensure they handle exactly as designed.
 Field Deployment: Lead and execute demanding on-site flight missions, sometimes lasting several weeks, under diverse weather and environmental conditions.
 Mission Safety & Logs: Rigorously follow test checklists, maintain safety protocols during high-throughput flight operations, and accurately report flight observations to the engineering, production and industrialisation teams.
 Candidate Requirements 
 Good RC/UAV Piloting Skills: You have extensive hands-on experience piloting RC planes, flying wings, or multirotor UAVs. Manual piloting dexterity and a deep instinct for flight mechanics are the absolute priorities for this role.
 Rigor & Endurance: Strong discipline to run repetitive, structured test cycles with consistent attention to detail and unwavering focus on safety.
 Adaptable Mindset: You thrive in fast-paced, lean startup environments where initiative, quick decision-making, and teamwork are valued over rigid hierarchy.
 Field-Ready & Mobile: You possess a valid driver’s license (Permis B) and are ready to drive team vehicles, transport flight gear/drones. You are looking for a highly active, hands-on role where you will be out in the field on a daily basis, all year round.
 Technical background: Any technical degree or professional experience in electronics, RC modeling, mechanics, or aeronautics is a great plus, but passionate self-taught pilots are highly encouraged to apply.
 Basic Technical English: Capable of understanding technical guidelines and writing flight reports in English.
 Nice-to-have 
 Certifications & FPV: Official drone pilot certifications, instructor ratings, or solid FPV (First Person View) racing/freestyle experience.
 Military or Field Background: Past experience in specialized military units or demanding field-oriented professions.
 Basic data/technical literacy: a basic grasp of autopilot systems, telemetry or flight-log reading, to help bridge the field and R&D. This is what turns an operator into a genuine validator, and is worth probing even if not required.

 About the role 
 Every airframe Harmattan AI flies starts with a model. System identification turns flight data into the verified dynamics that guidance and control are designed, tuned and trained on. It is the foundation of an autopilot that adapts across multirotors, fixed wings, VTOLs and missiles.
 As a System Identification Engineer, working out of Lausanne, you will own the path from flight test to identified model. You will design and run your own experiments, build a repeatable identification pipeline, and deliver models the G&C team can trust.
     Responsibilities 
 Experiment Design & Flight Test: Plan and run your own identification tests, from excitation design to flight tests, including coordinating with the .
 Model Identification: Identify rigid-body, aerodynamic, propulsion and actuator dynamics using frequency and time-domain methods, including closed-loop identification on vehicles flown under a controller.
 Propulsion & Actuators: Characterize motors, ESCs, propellers and control surfaces, including bandwidth, delays, saturation, and thermal and battery effects.
 Identification Pipeline: Build and maintain an automated, reproducible pipeline from flight logs to identified model. This covers ingestion, data-quality checks, estimation, validation and reporting.
 Model Validation: Validate models against held-out flight data, quantify uncertainty, and make sure each model is fit for purpose: controller design, simulation, or training learned G&C.
 New Airframes: Extend the capability from multirotors to control-surface multirotors, fixed wings, tail-sitters and missiles.
 Simulation & G&C Support: Deliver models into simulation, SITL and HITL, and work closely with control, guidance and embedded engineers to close the loop between models and flight results.
 Mentorship: Depending on seniority, support the team by mentoring junior engineers and interns.
     Candidate Requirements 
 Educational Background: A strong academic record with a degree in aerospace, control, mechanical engineering or a related STEM field. A practical track record matters more than the specific degree.
 System Identification: Proven experience identifying dynamic models of flying platforms from real data, in both the frequency and time domain, including the pitfalls of closed-loop data.
 Flight Mechanics & Control: Solid grasp of rigid-body dynamics, aerodynamic forces and moments, non-dimensionalization, stability modes and propulsion models. Also enough control background to know what the model will be used for.
 Flight Testing: Hands-on experience planning and running flight tests and working from raw, imperfect logs.
 Software: Strong Python and scientific computing skills, with the discipline to build tools others can rerun.
   Nice to have 
 Rigorous about data quality, uncertainty and validation; skeptical of models until they are proven.
 Autonomous and hands-on, comfortable moving between bench, field and code.
 Communicates clearly, able to present models and test results to engineers and senior stakeholders.
 Thrives under pressure in a fast-paced environment with a no-task-is-too-small mentality.
 Fixed-wing aerodynamic modeling; VTOL or tail-sitter dynamics; remote pilot certification; experience with real flight logs; structural or vibration modes; data-driven or learned dynamics models.
 Commitment: 100% dedication to Harmattan AI’s mission of providing a defensive edge to allied nations through ethical, high-impact technology.

items.jobTitle: CENTRALE LYON - Postdoctoral Researcher Position Deep Learning for Functional-Oxide Growth Video-to-Spectrum Prediction by RHEED / XRD Fusion
items.jobDescription:
PROJECT OVERVIEW 
 We are looking for a highly motivated Postdoctoral Researcher to develop innovative deeplearning models that predict the structure of functional-oxide thin films directly from their growth dynamics. Positioned at the interface between Artificial Intelligence and materials physics, the OXYD-IA project aims to design a deep model able to predict the final X-ray Diffraction (XRD) spectrum of an oxide thin film from the sole Reflection High-Energy Electron Diffraction (RHEED) video recorded during its growth by Molecular Beam Epitaxy (MBE). 
 The resulting tool will open the way to predictive, in situ control of oxide epitaxy – a process today dominated by a costly trial-and-error approach, in which the structural and functional properties of the films are only validated ex situ. You will join a genuinely multidisciplinary collaboration between the INL (Institut des Nanotechnologies de Lyon), which provides the operando experimental data and materials-physics expertise, and the LIRIS (équipe Imagine), which provides the deep video-learning and probabilistic-modelling methodology – both at École Centrale de Lyon. 
 A high-impact opportunity. AI for experimental physics is a fast-growing field, and OXYD-IA offers a genuine first-mover advantage within it: you would work on a unique, unpublished dataset of paired RHEED videos and XRD spectra to build one of the first video-to-spectrum models with calibrated uncertainty for oxide growth. By learning directly from experimental 1 data, such a model can short-circuit the traditional trial-and-error loop, accelerate discovery and drastically cut experimental time, cost, precursor consumption and instrument occupancy – turning routine in situ diagnostics into predictive tools. 
 Scientific context. Epitaxial perovskite-oxide thin films exhibit rich, tunable functional properties (thermoelectricity, ferroelectricity, piezoelectricity) governed by their structure and composition, themselves correlated with the growth conditions. MBE offers independent control of each element but, applied to oxides, is notoriously unstable and poorly reproducible because of the oxidising atmosphere. RHEED tracks the surface dynamics in real time (lattice parameter, surface reconstructions, roughness) but does not give access to the final bulk microstructure, which is only reachable ex situ via XRD / XRR. There is therefore a strong physical link – so far unexploited quantitatively – between RHEED dynamics and final XRD microstructure, which OXYD-IA proposes to learn directly.
 Figure 1 – OXYD-IA pipeline. At inference, the RHEED video acquired during growth (INL) feeds a deep video encoder (LIRIS) and a probabilistic regression module that predicts the final XRD spectrum together with its uncertainty. During training, the predicted spectrum is compared with the ex situ XRD / XRR spectrum measured at INL (ground truth); this discrepancy is the supervised learning signal that adjusts the model parameters.
 KEY RESEARCH AREAS AND RESPONSIBILITIES 
 You will drive the core computational research along a risk-managed, phased 12-month roadmap. The primary target is a versioned RHEED / XRD dataset, growth-regime classification and probabilistic regression of the key structural parameters with calibrated uncertainty; full-spectrum prediction, a real-time demonstrator and cross-oxide generalisation are stretch and follow-on objectives. The work is organised around three technical pillars: 
 1. Corpus structuring and spatio-temporal RHEED representation • Build a versioned dataset by cleaning, temporally aligning and pairing the RHEED video sequences, the associated MBE parameters (temperature, oxygen pressure, source fluxes) and the ex situ XRD / XRR spectra (SrTiO3 reference system). • Pre-train, in a self-supervised manner, a spatio-temporal video encoder (3D CNN, e.g. R(2+1)D, or temporal Vision Transformer) fine-tuned on the laboratory corpus. • Perform fuzzy / Bayesian classification of the growth regimes (2D vs. 3D modes, transitions, RHEED oscillations), building on LIRIS expertise in the statistical analysis of sequences. 
 2. Probabilistic RHEED →XRD regression with uncertainty quantification • Design a latent representation that couples the video encoding with the physical MBE parameters. • Learn stepwise – first scalar structural parameters (lattice parameter, density, mosaicity), more robust at small N, then the full 1D XRD spectrum. • Provide calibrated uncertainty estimates (Bayesian approaches or deep ensembles), indispensable for guiding real-time decisions during growth. 
 3. Real-time demonstrator and dissemination (stretch / follow-on) • Validate the model on new SrTiO3 growths and prototype an in-growth inference tool at the end of the NANOFUTUR MBE line. • Mitigate the small-data and generalisation challenges through temporal data augmentation, transfer learning from pre-trained video encoders and domain adaptation towards other functional oxides. • Contribute toward a high-impact joint publication at the AI / materials interface (the project milestone is the submission of a joint paper).
 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 
 • A Ph.D. in the field of Artificial Intelligence – Computer Science, Machine Learning, Computer Vision or Signal Processing, and we are looking for a senior postdoc with 2–5 years of post-PhD experience. 
 • Deep learning on sequential / video data: demonstrable, hands-on experience with 3D CNNs, temporal transformers and / or probabilistic models. Proficiency in Python and PyTorch (or TensorFlow) is mandatory. 
 • A genuine appetite for physics: a strong curiosity for, or prior exposure to, experimental physics and materials science. The ideal candidate carried out an AI-focused Ph.D. and is eager to apply it to a real materials-physics problem. 
 • Research mindset: a track record of innovation and the ability to work autonomously on a complex, multidisciplinary project. • Software skills: experience with Git version control and reproducible research. 
 • Excellent communication and scientific-writing skills in English. 
 ADDITIONAL SKILLS AND COMPETENCIES 
 • Self-supervised video pre-training, uncertainty quantification (Bayesian / ensembles), fuzzy classification, or domain adaptation. 
 • Experience with small-sample / transfer-learning settings and handling large-scale experimental datasets.
 HOW TO APPLY 
 Please prepare a single PDF file containing: 
 1. A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including a list of publications. 
 2. A 1-page motivation letter explaining your specific interest in this project and how your background addresses the key responsibilities and qualifications listed above. 
 3. The names and contact information of at least two academic references.

About Us 
 ClearBank is a technology-enabled bank transforming banking infrastructure through innovative technology and a full banking licence. We provide cloud-based banking and payment solutions to a growing range of clients and are committed to delivering reliable, scalable financial services while maintaining the highest standards of financial control, governance and regulatory compliance.
 The Financial Control team is responsible for ensuring ClearBank’s general ledgers are controlled, maintained and reconciled to support timely and accurate reporting across the organisation and externally to regulators and tax authorities. As ClearBank continues to grow, the team plays a critical role in building scalable, efficient and well-controlled finance processes that support the Bank’s strategic ambitions.
 Role Purpose 
 The Financial Control Lead owns allocated month-end activities within a small, hands-on team, supporting accurate, timely and well-controlled financial information.
 Reporting to the Financial Control Manager, you will complete month-end tasks, investigate balances and variances, and prepare accounting entries and reconciliations to keep the general ledger accurate and fully supported.
 The role will also be expected to stay close to all key aspects of the Financial Control team’s remit, including journals, reconciliations, reporting inputs, controls, audit support, process documentation and stakeholder queries. As ClearBank continues to grow, the Financial Control Lead will be at the forefront of identifying, driving and implementing scalable, efficient and well-controlled processes, helping the team reduce manual effort while maintaining strong financial control standards.
 Key Responsibilities 
 Financial Control & Reporting 
 Own allocated month-end close activities and ensure they are delivered accurately and on time.
 Prepare, review and approve general ledger journals as required, ensuring postings are technically accurate, appropriately supported and comply with internal control requirements.
 Own revenue and expense analysis for the relevant areas, ensuring variances are investigated, understood and appropriately communicated to stakeholders.
 Own the monthly capitalisation and amortisation process for intangible assets, ensuring entries are accurate, supported and appropriately controlled.
 Partner with Financial Planning & Analysis to ensure accruals and accounting adjustments are identified, calculated and recorded accurately.
 Prepare, review and approve bank reconciliations as required, ensuring reconciling items are investigated and resolved promptly.
 Own monthly balance sheet reconciliations for the relevant areas, including preparing and reviewing reconciliations where required, ensuring all balances are fully supported and outstanding issues are appropriately managed.
 Take ownership of non-automated accounting entries, ensuring they are accurate, appropriately supported, controlled and clearly documented, with clear audit trails maintained.
 Build and implement scalable, efficient processes while remaining hands-on in day-to-day delivery where needed.
 Support the preparation of management, regulatory, statutory and tax reporting requirements as required.
 Ensure compliance with accounting policies, financial reporting standards and internal control frameworks
 Systems, Automation & Continuous Improvement 
 Help drive and implement automation and process improvements across finance processes, controls and reporting activities, helping to reduce manual effort and improve scalability.
 Lead initiatives to automate the capture and posting of accounting entries from ClearBank’s core banking and operational systems into the general ledger.
 Identify opportunities to improve efficiency, scalability and data quality across Financial Control processes.
 Drive the adoption of AI-enabled tools and technologies to reduce manual effort, improve accuracy and enhance team productivity.
 Ensure process changes are documented appropriately and supported by effective control frameworks.
 Stakeholder Management 
 Build strong working relationships across Finance and the wider business to support accurate financial reporting and operational effectiveness.
 Work collaboratively with Accounts Payable, FP&A, Tax, Treasury, Regulatory Reporting and external auditors to ensure reporting requirements are met.
 Support audit activities by coordinating information requests and providing timely, accurate responses.
 Contribute to cross-functional projects requiring accounting, control or process expertise.
 What success looks like in the role: 
 Month-end reporting processes are delivered accurately, on time and in line with agreed timetables.
 The general ledger remains well-controlled, supported and reconciled, with minimal audit findings or control weaknesses.
 Complex accounting areas, including share-based payments, are supported with accurate analysis, appropriate documentation and clear escalation where technical judgement is required.
 Practical capex accounting experience is applied to ensure capitalisation and amortisation are accurate, well-supported and appropriately controlled as part of the wider Financial Control remit.
 Financial control processes become increasingly automated, scalable and efficient as ClearBank grows.
 AI-enabled tools are successfully adopted to improve productivity, insight and operational effectiveness.
 Stakeholders receive accurate, timely and reliable financial information that supports decision-making and reporting obligations.
 The role works effectively with colleagues across Finance and the wider business to deliver high-quality outcomes.
 Financial Control contributes to a strong control environment while continuously improving efficiency and reducing operational risk.
 The role demonstrates excellence in both what is delivered and how it is delivered through strong collaboration, ownership, continuous improvement and leadership behaviours.
 Skills & Experience (must-have) 
 Fully qualified accountant (ACA, ACCA or CIMA).
 Strong financial accounting and financial control experience within a regulated financial services environment.
 Experience managing month-end close activities, balance sheet reconciliations and general ledger controls.
 Experience managing the monthly capitalisation and amortisation of intangible assets, including accurate accounting entries, supporting documentation and financial controls.
 Strong technical accounting knowledge, including experience interpreting and applying accounting standards.
 Experience supporting complex accounting areas, including preparing analysis and documentation to support technical accounting judgements.
 Strong understanding of financial controls, governance and audit requirements.
 Proven ability to identify, lead and implement process improvement initiatives.
 Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and strong financial analysis capability.
 Strong stakeholder management and communication skills.
 Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and evolving environment.
 High attention to detail combined with a pragmatic and solutions-focused mindset.
 A little bit more about us!  
 ClearBank is Where You Can belong:  
 At ClearBank we think about Diversity, Equity and Inclusion (DE&I) a lot. Not because we think we should. But because we know we should – how else can we build a happy workforce and be successful as a business. We’re committed to making sure our teams reflect society. And we put energy and effort into making this a place where everyone feels at home, where they’re given the trust and encouragement to do their very best work. Here are some of the things we’re most proud of:

 Our hiring process and what you can expect:

 Screening: You’ll spend 30-45 minutes speaking to one of our recruiters learning more about the role and ClearBank, and we’ll get it know more about you, your experience and how your skills align with the role (this will be via phone or Teams video call). You can expect to hear back from us within seven days following this meeting (if things are taking longer than expected, we’ll let you know that too);

About Fractile 
 Fractile was founded in 2022 on the bet that, eventually, the world’s most capable AI systems would be limited in their impact by the time taken to produce useful outputs. We bet everything on the logical conclusion: that the only way to truly unlock this latent value, to make speed viable at scale, was to radically re-invent the hardware that we run our frontier AI models on. Ever since, we have been building chips and systems that tackle this problem: how to efficiently generate output at thousands of tokens per second, while handling the complexity and capacity challenges of operating large models at very long contexts.
   The workloads that push to the limits of the current frontier are already transformational; it is the technical and economic limits on inference speed that are constraining progress. The defining work of the 21st century will be marked by the engine of inference delivering immense and diffuse chains of intellectual inquiry, in drug discovery, in software engineering, in materials discovery, in any field where progress is driven by deep reasoning and intelligence to resolve complex problems. 
 About the Software organisation at Fractile
 Developer Experience sits within the Software organisation at Fractile, which is responsible for developing a full software stack for our groundbreaking AI inference systems. That's everything from ML compilers, device drivers and systems firmware, application level runtime and ecosystem integrations, ML and compute libraries, great developer tooling and a full portfolio of simulators, through to datacenter scale workload deployment solutions. At Fractile, we know that a fantastic software stack is a critical and central part of any AI inference solution and it sits at the heart of everything we're doing.
About the team and role
 The tools built by the Developer Experience team are how engineers — both inside Fractile and at our customers — see, control and understand the Fractile inference accelerator. That means the command-line utilities used to discover, configure and health-check devices; the diagnostics used during hardware bring-up and in the datacentre; and the profiling, tracing and debugging tools that show where the time goes across the host, the driver and the silicon.
 As a Tools Developer you will design and build these tools in Rust, running on Linux hosts from a single developer workstation against large datacentre deployments. You will work closely with the hardware, firmware, kernel driver, runtime and Developer Experience teams to understand what they need, and turn that into fast, reliable and well-designed tools that fit naturally into existing Linux workflows. This is largely greenfield work, with real scope to shape how our tooling is architected and how it is used.
About you
 You enjoy building tools that other engineers rely on every day, and you care about getting the details right: clear output, sensible defaults, good error messages and behaviour you can script against. You are at home on Linux, comfortable working anywhere from the shell down to sysfs, ioctls and the kernel/userspace boundary, and you know how to find out what a system is actually doing when it misbehaves. You are self-driven, able to identify tooling opportunities for yourself, and happy to work autonomously in areas of ambiguity.
Key Requirements
 Strong Rust skills, with experience shipping production-quality tools or libraries
 Knowledge of Linux from a developer's perspective: processes, memory, filesystems, sysfs/procfs, device files and ioctls, systemd and the kernel/userspace interface
 Experience designing command-line tools and APIs that are easy to learn, script and automate
 Experience working with stakeholders across multiple teams
